references.text: God gives Moses instructions to build the tabernacle exactly according to the pattern shown to him on the mountain.
It repeats that the Israelites did everything just as the Lord had commanded Moses, and Moses blessed them for their obedience.
Moses completed the work on the tabernacle, confirming the completion mentioned in 39:32.
Moses calls all skilled workers to come and make everything the Lord has commanded.
Bezalel, Oholiab, and all the skilled men begin the work according to the Lord's command.
The Israelites did everything just as the Lord had commanded Moses - the same formula of obedience.
Heaven and earth were completed - parallel to the completion of the tabernacle as God's dwelling place on earth.
The book of Hebrews refers to Moses being warned to make everything according to the pattern shown to him on the mountain.
It describes the furnishings of the tabernacle that were made according to God's instructions to Moses.
Stephen mentions that our ancestors had the tent of testimony in the wilderness, made according to the pattern Moses had seen.
This is a direct summary of the same event as the source verse and serves as double testimony to the completion.
It connects the obedience shown in building the tent with later obedience regarding camp placement and departure in the wilderness.
It complements the people's obedience with Moses' own complete obedience in carrying out God's commands.
It establishes a theological pattern where collective obedience at the festivals mirrors the obedience shown in building the sanctuary.
It creates a theological arc showing that the same principle of obedience that built the tent also led to entering the promised land.
It links the obedience shown in building the tabernacle to the subsequent obedience in consecrating the Levites for service.
